items.followUp: State one difference between somatic cells and germline cells.

rubric.why: Identifies somatic cells as body cells rather than cells involved in reproduction.
rubric.description: Somatic cells make up the body and are not involved in producing gametes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying somatic cells as body or non-reproductive cells.

rubric.why: Identifies germline cells as cells involved in reproduction and gamete formation.
rubric.description: Germline cells are reproductive cells that give rise to gametes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that germline cells are reproductive cells or give rise to gametes.

modelAnswer: Somatic cells are the non-reproductive cells that make up the body.
Germline cells are reproductive cells that give rise to gametes.

items.followUp: What two types of reactions make up metabolism?

rubric.why: Defines metabolism as the total set of chemical reactions.
rubric.description: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions occurring in an organism or its cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining metabolism as the sum or total of chemical reactions in an organism or its cells.

rubric.why: Identifies both major categories of metabolic reactions.
rubric.description: Metabolism includes anabolic (building-up) and catabolic (breaking-down) reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both anabolism and catabolism, or describing both building-up and breaking-down reactions.

modelAnswer: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions occurring in an organism or its cells.
It includes both building-up (anabolic) and breaking-down (catabolic) reactions.

items.followUp: What is a cofactor, and how does it help an enzyme?

rubric.why: Identifies a co-enzyme as an organic, non-protein molecule.
rubric.description: A co-enzyme is a small organic, non-protein molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a co-enzyme is organic and non-protein.

rubric.why: Explains that a co-enzyme assists an enzyme's function.
rubric.description: A co-enzyme associates with an enzyme and helps it carry out its function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a co-enzyme associates with or helps an enzyme to function.

modelAnswer: A co-enzyme is a small organic, non protein molecule.
It associates with an enzyme and helps the enzyme carry out its function.
